findings.title: On the phone the page does not reflow, so the booking form is mostly off the screen

location.description: the whole page at phone width: hero text, nav, and booking form

findings.viewer_experience: A phone visitor sees only a sliver of the form and must scroll sideways to book. The hero text is squeezed into a 119 px column and the nav stacks into five lines.

current.value: page 587 px wide in a 390 px viewport; p.lead 9.1 characters per line

findings.target: page width equal to the 390 px viewport, with everything in one column and the form fully on screen
findings.fix_direction: Below tablet width, stack everything into one column: headline, intro, form, then routes. Give the nav a phone treatment that fits on one row or folds away.

closed_when.check: page_width in the phone viewport is 390 or less, and p.lead characters_per_line in the phone viewport is 30 or more

findings.title: Nothing leads, because the headline is styled as the weakest text in the hero

location.description: the h1 headline above the intro

findings.viewer_experience: The darker intro paragraph wins over the pale headline, so the visitor has no clear first line to read and the offer takes a second pass to find.

current.value: h1 22 px, weight 400, gray #6b7574; p.lead 20 px near-black; nav 20 px; logo 24 px

findings.target: a headline that is clearly the first thing seen: a real step up in size, in dark color, and a nav smaller than the lead
findings.fix_direction: Make the headline a real step larger and dark, perhaps a heavier weight or the serif from the logo. Bring the nav down toward 16 px so it stops matching the lead.
findings.source: Bringhurst 3.1.1; Dair chapters 8 and 9; Tschichold, The New Typography

closed_when.check: h1 font_size is clearly larger than p.lead font_size and the logo, h1 color has contrast of 4.5 or more, and nav.site-nav font_size is below p.lead font_size, in the desktop, tablet, phone and widescreen viewports

findings.title: Two buttons do the same job, and the stronger style is on the weaker one

location.description: the filled hero button "See boats and dates"; the form's outlined "Search" button is the other

findings.viewer_experience: The visitor has to stop and work out which button to press, and whether the left one ignores what they set in the form.

current.value: hero link filled, form Search outlined; both lead to available boats

findings.target: one booking action, with the form's Search as the filled primary
findings.fix_direction: Keep one action. Make the form's Search the filled primary, and remove the hero button or give it a different job.
findings.source: Material Design emphasis levels; Nielsen heuristic 8

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees the form's Search as the one filled primary button, and the hero button is gone or has a clearly different job.

findings.title: The copy buries the reason to book here, and the headline contradicts the routes

location.description: the headline and the intro text under it

findings.viewer_experience: A skimming visitor stops before the direct-booking point at the end of the intro. "For a week" clashes with the 4-night and 10-night routes. "No fee on top of the hire" has no price to measure against, so the visitor must take it on trust.

current.value: headline "Hire a narrowboat for a week on the canal"; direct-booking claim in the last sentence of the intro; no hire price shown

findings.target: the direct-booking point in the headline or the line straight under it, no "for a week" clash with the routes, and a fact that proves the claim
findings.fix_direction: Move the direct-booking point up into the headline or the line straight under it, and drop or loosen "for a week". Show the kind of fact that proves the claim, such as a from-price per week. The boatyard must supply that figure.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees the direct-booking point in the headline or the line under it, no "for a week" clash with the route list, and a boatyard-supplied fact that backs the no-fee claim.

findings.title: On wide screens the page splits to the edges and leaves a hole in the middle

location.description: the space between the text column and the form, and the dead band under the hero button

findings.viewer_experience: The eye must cross about 850 px of nothing to get from the pitch to the form at 1920 px, and the form looks like a sidebar instead of the point of the page. At 1280 px a dead band of about 270 px sits above the routes.

current.value: text column ends at x 664 and form starts at x 1539 at 1920 px; about 270 px dead band at 1280 px

findings.target: text and form sit as one group, with the gap above the routes closed
findings.fix_direction: Put the layout in a max-width container so the text and the form sit as one group, and close the gap above the routes.
findings.source: Arnheim on balance; Ruder on gathered space

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees the text and the form as one group in the desktop and widescreen viewports, with no wide empty band between them and none above the routes.

findings.title: A holiday page with no picture of the holiday

location.description: the whole hero, which shows no boat and no water

findings.viewer_experience: People hire a narrowboat for the boat and the water, and the page shows neither.
findings.target: a real photo of the boatyard's own boats or a stretch of a route
findings.fix_direction: Add a real photo of the boatyard's own boats or a stretch of a route, and avoid stock pictures. The boatyard must supply the photo.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees a real photo of a boat or a route on the page, and it does not look like stock.

findings.title: The h1 and the gray route details are just under 4.5:1

location.description: the gray route details such as "7 nights, 38 locks" (the h1 has the same color)

findings.viewer_experience: The gray text is slightly too faint for low-vision readers.
findings.fix_direction: Darken the gray slightly. The headline fix in finding 2 covers the h1.

closed_when.check: contrast of the route detail spans (ul > li > span:nth-of-type(2)) and h1 in the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen viewports is 4.5 or more

findings.title: The form field borders are pale gray on white

location.description: the start-date field, where the border is the only edge

findings.viewer_experience: The fields are hard to see as fields, and the start-date field has no other edge.
findings.target: border contrast of at least 3:1 against the white form
findings.fix_direction: Darken the field borders to at least 3:1.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees clearly visible field borders on the form in all viewports, judged to be at least 3:1 against white.

findings.title: On the tablet the intro runs 24 characters per line and ends with "hire." alone

location.description: the intro paragraph on the tablet

findings.viewer_experience: The narrow column makes the intro choppy and leaves a single word on the last line.
findings.target: at least 45 characters per line, with no single-word last line
findings.fix_direction: Widen the text column or narrow the gap to the form.

closed_when.check: p.lead characters_per_line in the tablet viewport is 45 or more

findings.title: On the phone the route rows break a number from its unit

location.description: the route detail "4 nights, 12 locks" on the phone, which wraps to two lines

findings.viewer_experience: A number such as "12" sits at the end of a line and its unit "locks" starts the next.

current.value: route details wrap to 2 lines, separating number and unit

findings.target: each number and its unit on the same line
findings.fix_direction: Join each number and unit with a non-breaking space, or stack the details under the route name.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees no route detail in the phone viewport where a number is split from its unit across lines.

findings.title: "Sat 14 June" looks like a free-text field, not a date picker

location.description: the start-date field in the form

findings.viewer_experience: The visitor cannot tell whether to type a date or pick one.

current.value: a plain text-looking field holding "Sat 14 June"

findings.target: a date input or picker if the field takes typed text
findings.fix_direction: If it takes typed text, constrain it to a date input or picker.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees the start-date field as a date input or picker, not free text.
